h1:
Khon Kaen Dessert & Bakery Cafés
11 Spots That Are Genuinely Good
intro: Khon Kaen isn't only about laab and som tam — the city's dessert scene runs deeper than most people expect. There are homemade cake shops in old wooden houses, fresh-baked croissant cafés where people line up from opening, serious French bakeries, and Thai sweets plus ice cream for pocket change at Ton Tan Market in the evening. We've picked 11 spots that actually taste good, not just look good — a mix of cake places, French-style bakeries, Thai sweets and ice cream, each with the area, a rough price range and where to take photos, so you can plan a dessert run through Khon Kaen without a wasted stop.

blocks.html: Khon Kaen's desserts fall into four broad camps. The first is homemade cake shops and dessert cafés that bake fresh on site — many sit in old wooden houses or prettily styled buildings you can photograph. The second is French-style bakeries and patisseries doing serious croissants, tarts and baked goods. The third is Thai sweets and traditional desserts you'll find around the markets. And the fourth is ice cream and light, heat-beating treats that cost next to nothing. This list mixes all four so you can pick by mood. The prices listed are rough ranges from the latest menus and may shift by branch and fruit season.

We ranked mainly on taste and consistency, then atmosphere and photo corners, then how easy each place is to reach. A spot near the bottom of the list hasn't lost — some are traditional, local places or just sit outside the city centre. Honestly, the well-known homemade cake shops in Khon Kaen get packed on weekends and the popular menu items sell out fast, so we've noted what to know for each one.

blocks.text: Ranking: Khon Kaen's dessert & cake cafés

items.name: Mali Cakery (Mali Cakery Homemade)
items.blurb: A homemade cake shop in a two-storey white wooden house in an old-fashioned style, with a garden wrapping the building — every corner photographs well, which is why it's become a pin for dessert lovers in Khon Kaen. Cakes are baked fresh on site daily. The signature is a jasmine tea fragrant with real jasmine flowers, served in a glass teapot, alongside slices like Strawberry Shortcake and coconut pie. Nothing is cloyingly sweet — the sweetness is well controlled. It's the best balance of taste and atmosphere in the city.
items.meta: In Khon Kaen city · Old wooden house with a garden · Consistently high review ratings

items.name: Trinity Café — Head Office, Na Mueang Road
items.blurb: Khon Kaen's famous croissant café, decorated open and airy in white, with an open kitchen where you can watch the baking and the smell of butter filling the room. The standouts are fresh-baked croissants and flat croissants done in batches, well-stuffed onigiri-style pastries, egg tarts and croffles. People queue from opening and the popular items sell out fast. There are several branches in the city — if you want the full menu, go to the Na Mueang branch in the morning.
items.meta: Na Mueang Road · City centre · Several branches

items.name: Pan Paeng Bake a Cake
items.blurb: A cake and baked-goods shop that gets a lot of reviews from locals in Khon Kaen. The cakes are decorated nicely and photograph well for social media. The standouts are a blueberry cheesecake and a dense chocolate cake that plenty of reviews say you have to order. The taste is consistent, making it good for a birthday cake or for sitting in. It's another safe choice for a cake shop in the city.
items.meta: In Khon Kaen city · Cake & baked-goods shop
items.price: Cake slice ~฿90–160 · Whole cakes to order

items.name: Café de Paris
items.blurb: A French-style café in Khon Kaen city focused on baked goods and European breakfasts — French pastries, baked bread and oeufs cocotte. The atmosphere is relaxed, like a café in Paris. It suits people who are serious about French bakery and want to linger over a long breakfast, sipping coffee with a pastry.
items.meta: In Khon Kaen city · French-style café

items.name: Sri Brown Cafe' — Kangsadan area
items.blurb: A dessert café in the Kangsadan area near the university. The standouts are hot toast with several toppings and Thai-tea / green-tea crepes, and plenty of reviews single out the caramel milkshake as a must-try. The vibe is friendly, student-café style, the prices are light, and it's good for a chilled afternoon stop or a dessert after a meal.
items.meta: Kangsadan area · Near Khon Kaen University

items.name: Gustoso Dessert & Pastries
items.blurb: A dessert and patisserie shop making a range of cakes and pastries. The one people talk about is the Masai, a soft-textured chocolate cake, and there are plenty of options in the case. It suits anyone who wants French-style cakes with lots of choice in one place. Honestly, reviews swing a bit depending on the item and the time you go — we'd suggest sticking to the signatures to be safe.
items.meta: In Khon Kaen city · Dessert & patisserie shop

items.name: Crusty Bakehouse — Kanlapaphruek Road
items.blurb: A newly opened bakery café on Kanlapaphruek Road, across from the Demonstration School. The standout is a wide range of baked goods made fresh daily — bread, pastries and cakes, with lots to choose from. It opens early, so it's good for grabbing baked goods for breakfast or to take home. Open Monday–Sunday 08:00–17:00, occasionally closed Mondays, so check the times before you go.
items.meta: Kanlapaphruek Road · Across from the Demonstration School · Open ~08:00–17:00

items.name: Engmore Crafthouse KKC — Sila sub-district
items.blurb: A dessert café decorated in Japanese style inside a Japanese garden in Sila sub-district — shady, leafy and photogenic. The standouts are matcha, green tea and cocoa drinks plus a bael-fruit cake that's the signature. It suits matcha fans and anyone after a calm setting to sit and sip tea over cake for a while. Open 10:00–17:00, closed Tuesdays, so check the times before you drive out.
items.meta: Sila sub-district · Japanese garden · Open 10:00–17:00, closed Tue

items.name: Times Square
items.blurb: An ice cream and waffle dessert spot in the city, with several ice cream flavours, waffles and heat-beating treats like mango sticky rice ice cream in fruit season. It's good for a cold dessert on a hot afternoon, and the prices are friendly. An easy choice for a family or a group of friends who want to share ice cream and waffles together.
items.meta: In Khon Kaen city · Ice cream & waffle shop

items.name: Thai sweets at Ton Tan Market (Wan Wan + Bonito Ice Cream)
items.blurb: If you want Thai sweets and ice cream for pocket change, Ton Tan Market in the evening is the answer. The Wan Wan / Ban Khao Nom stall makes Thai sweets like khanom chan, mango sticky rice and khanom tom, all nicely presented, while Bonito Ice Cream serves ice cream and smoothies in plenty of flavours at local prices. You can graze across several stalls in one place. A good way to close the day with cheap, traditional desserts.
items.meta: Ton Tan Market · Open evening–night, ~17:00 onwards

items.name: Chai Maha Bakery
items.blurb: A traditional bakery that's been open for over 30 years. The standout is an old-recipe orange cake that many reviews say isn't too sweet — nicely balanced. It's a homey kind of dessert, not a freshly styled café, and the prices are easy. It suits anyone who likes old-recipe cakes with a familiar taste, whether to eat on the spot or carry home as a simple gift.
items.meta: In Khon Kaen city · Long-running bakery, 30+ years

blocks.title: Tips to dodge the queues and sold-out items
blocks.html: Croissant places like Trinity Café get a queue from opening and the popular items sell out fast — if you want the full spread, go shortly after opening in the morning. Homemade cake shops like Mali Cakery and Pan Paeng get packed on weekend afternoons and evenings, and the popular slices may run out, so aim for before midday. Cafés outside the city centre like Engmore in Sila and Crusty on Kanlapaphruek — check their closing days and opening hours before you drive out. As for Thai sweets at Ton Tan Market, it opens evening to night, so come early evening for the full selection and cooler air.

blocks.text: How to pick, by the mood you're after

items: Want both taste and photos in one place — Mali Cakery, a wooden house with a garden, fresh-baked cake and jasmine tea, photogenic from every corner
For croissants and fresh-baked bakery — Trinity Café on Na Mueang Road, go early before things sell out, or Crusty Bakehouse on Kanlapaphruek
For French cakes and patisserie — Café de Paris for French pastries, or Gustoso for chocolate cake and lots of choice
For matcha and a calm setting — Engmore Crafthouse in the Japanese garden in Sila, good for lingering
For cheap Thai sweets and ice cream — Thai sweets and Bonito at Ton Tan Market in the evening, or old-recipe orange cake at Chai Maha Bakery

blocks.html: Most of these places are within Khon Kaen city, easy to reach by car or ride-hailing app. Central spots like Mali Cakery, Pan Paeng, Café de Paris and the Na Mueang branch of Trinity Café sit near the Bueng Kaen Nakhon area and Na Mueang Road, so they're convenient. Sri Brown is in the Kangsadan area near Khon Kaen University, Engmore is in Sila sub-district, and Crusty is on Kanlapaphruek Road — those take a little driving out of the city centre. Budget per dessert plate is mostly around ฿60–200, with French cakes and patisserie possibly higher, while Thai sweets and ice cream at Ton Tan Market are far cheaper, from a few dozen baht to under a hundred. Allow about an hour per place if you're sitting in.

faq.q: Which Khon Kaen dessert shop is the most photogenic and tastes best?
faq.a: If you want both taste and photos in one place, Mali Cakery (Mali Cakery Homemade) ranks at the top — a two-storey white wooden house with a garden all around, photogenic from every corner, with cakes baked fresh daily. The signature is a jasmine tea fragrant with real jasmine. Cake slices run about ฿129–169 and drinks about ฿100–139.

faq.q: Where do I go for fresh-baked croissants in Khon Kaen?
faq.a: Trinity Café is Khon Kaen's famous croissant café, with its head-office branch on Na Mueang Road and an open kitchen where you can watch the baking. The standouts are croissants, flat croissants, onigiri-style pastries and egg tarts. People queue from opening and the popular items sell out fast, so go in the morning. Croissants and pastries run about ฿80–140.

faq.q: Where can I get cheap Thai sweets and ice cream in Khon Kaen?
faq.a: Ton Tan Market in the evening is a one-stop spot. The Wan Wan / Ban Khao Nom stall makes Thai sweets like khanom chan, mango sticky rice and khanom tom, and Bonito Ice Cream serves ice cream and smoothies in plenty of flavours at local prices. Most prices run from a few dozen baht to under a hundred. The market opens evening to night.

faq.q: Are there serious French bakery and cake shops in Khon Kaen?
faq.a: Yes — Café de Paris makes French pastries and European breakfasts like oeufs cocotte, and Gustoso Dessert & Pastries is known for the soft Masai chocolate cake and a range of pastries. For fresh-baked bakery there's Crusty Bakehouse on Kanlapaphruek Road, baking fresh every day.

faq.q: Which Khon Kaen dessert café is best for matcha and a garden setting?
faq.a: Engmore Crafthouse KKC in Sila sub-district, decorated in Japanese style inside a Japanese garden. The standouts are matcha, green tea, cocoa and a bael-fruit cake, and the setting is shady and photogenic. Open 10:00–17:00, closed Tuesdays — check the times before you drive out, as it's outside the city centre.
